pulls.title: Incorporate changes discussed in IETF 122 hackathon
pulls.author: TheEnbyperor
pulls.body:
This is a bit of a big PR, so apologies first.

The main purpose of this is to incorporate the changes we discussed at the hackathon, and tidy up a few bits, to make the draft easier to follow. 

- Clarify encoding of messages, as two concatenated CBOR objects
- Add "Available PKIDs" to allow for the server to help select authenticators if multiple are present
- Add "Acceptable hash algorithms" and "Hash algorithm" for crypto agility; this is supported even on the windows `webauthn.h` platform authenticator (with SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512).
- Add tables defining which attributes can be encoded in which messages
- Add an example protocol flow diagram
- Define error codes, as a first attempt
- Add a reference to my FreeRadius implementation
- Define IANA registries

I've also added myself as an author, hope that's OK.

Finally: given we now have two interoperable implementations I think it's time we request IANA register a method number. As 1-191 are merely specification required there's no reason not to do this with an I-D.

comments.body: This is actually a CBOR sequence, since CBOR sequence is defined as the concatenation of CBOR data items (see RFC 8742)

It appears, that I conflated CBOR lists and CBOR sequences. Oops!

I guess here is an idea place to put a reference to what a CBOR sequence is then.
Yep, I've already added it in my local working document, I'll push an update to the document soon.
